title: Global Operations Center / Digital Operations Team
publicPositioning: Digital workers, AI Manager, AI Director and operations roles are platform capabilities and managed operational functions. They must not be presented as verified human employees unless a real person is identified and authorized.

roles.label: AI Manager
roles.authority: prepare, classify, summarize, validate checklist state
roles.limits: no final legal, financial, employment, deployment or mass communication decision

roles.label: AI Director
roles.authority: coordinate workflows, surface conflicts, recommend priorities
roles.limits: no claim of human executive authority

roles.label: Executive Office
roles.authority: final approval route and decision record
roles.limits: must be linked to real authorized decision-maker for binding actions

roles.label: Supervisory Board View
roles.authority: review status, risk and audit summaries
roles.limits: read/review unless formal approval is granted

roles.label: Digital Operations Workers / Wave 1
roles.authority: content preparation, data checks, publishing support, CRM/media support

roles.label: Digital Operations Workers / Wave 2
roles.authority: expanded multilingual, market, registry, media and support workflows
roles.limits: must follow approval queue and source-evidence rules

corePolicies: Transparency: do not imply that AI roles are real human employees.
Accountability: every binding action requires a human-authorized approval state.
Traceability: every output must link to source, preview, requester and decision record when possible.
Least privilege: workers receive only the permissions required for the task.
No mass send: communication workers may prepare and validate, but sending requires explicit approval.
No production deploy: technical workers may prepare checks and notes, but deploy requires executive confirmation.
Public accuracy: public pages must distinguish existing entities, planned entities, digital roles and strategic projects.
